content: We need to find template that when applied to the given molecule (target) reproduces the Peterson reaction retrosynthesis: product is the given molecule (alkene with two phenyl OMe groups). The forward reaction forms C=C double bond, breaks C-Si and C-O bonds, forming C=C and losing ketone? Actually description: Peterson Reaction: alpha-silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl, forms beta-hydroxy silane, then elimination yields alkene, losing Si and OH (forming carbonyl? Actually product is alkene, starting from carbonyl + silyl carbanion). In retrosynthesis, we break C=C double bond to form carbonyl (ketone) and trimethylsilyl group attached to carbon (i.e., silyl carbanion precursor). So we need template that breaks C=C double bond and forms ketone and trimethylsilyl. Functional groups broken: C-C double bonds. Formed: ketones, trimethylsilyl. We attempted search with those criteria but got no results. Maybe need to specify bonds broken/formed. The description: carbon-silicon bond broken, carbon-oxygen bond broken, carbon-carbon double bond formed. In forward reaction, C-C double bond formed, C-Si broken, C-O broken. In retrosynthesis, we need to break C=C (i.e., functional group broken: C-C double bonds) and form ketone and trimethylsilyl. Our search gave empty. Maybe need to use bonds criteria.
